newsitem.title: USA: Basic cable ad revs up 24.1 pct - trade group.
newsitem.headline: Basic cable ad revs up 24.1 pct - trade group.

text.p: Advertising revenue on basic cable television networks grew 24.1 percent to $4.28 billion from October 1995 through September 1996, the Cabletelevision Advertising Bureau said Wednesday.
The trade group said that increase far outpaces advertising growth among other media.

"Basic cable's advertising revenues are growing faster than those of any other medium because ad dollars follow viewers, and our medium's total day viewing share has hit 34 and will climb even higher," bureau President and Chief Executive Joe Ostrow said in a statement.

The association said the runner-up was national newspapers, which saw advertising revenue grow by 18.2 percent, while broadcast network television ad revenues grew by 17.9 percent and network radio ad revenues jumped 17.2 percent.
